chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Four categories of people must perform the complete prayer, whether they are traveling or resident: the Mukari, the Karri, the Ra'i, and the Ash-taqan, because their work is [continuous].'

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: Complete prayer (performing all four rak'ahs without shortening to two)
key_terms.السَّفَر: Travel (journey where shortening prayer is normally permitted)
key_terms.الْأَشْتَقَانُ: A specific category of worker (often identified as a weaver or artisan)
key_terms.الْكَرِيُّ: A specific category of worker (likely a porter or laborer)
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: A specific category of worker (likely a carrier or transporter)
key_terms.حَضَر: Residence/Home (where full prayer is normally performed)

ai.seo_question: Who are the four categories of people required to perform complete prayers during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that the Mukari (carrier), Karri (porter), Ra'i (herdsman), and Ash-taqan (weaver) are exempt from shortening prayers due to the nature of their labor, which often involves continuous activity or staying in one location. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the hardship or specific conditions of one's occupation can override the general rule of Qasr prayer during travel, emphasizing practicality in worship.
